extracted.intended_audience: AAAI-26 reviewers (human reviewers, Area Chairs, Senior Program Committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing professional, constructive, and evaluative reviews for submissions to the AAAI-26 Main Technical Track, including what to check about claims, contributions, presentation, evaluations, and how to use or respond to AI-generated reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depersonalized, respectful tone
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, please do not use “I”, “you”, “the authors”, etc., in your reviews. Reviews should be depersonalized as much as possible. Use terms like “the paper”, “the work”, “the project”. The review should focus on the work and not the individuals (reviewers or authors). Avoid referring to yourself. If you must refer to yourself, it should be in the third person (e.g., “this reviewer”) and done sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase comments as would be appropriate if you were speaking respectfully to the authors face-to-face. Keep language professional and avoid personal attacks or ad hominem. This helps maintain constructive feedback and reduces perceived hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive framing (ask how to improve)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of “What is wrong with this paper?”, ask yourself “How could this paper be better?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable suggestions rather than only negative statements. Where possible, propose concrete steps, clarifications, experiments, or analyses that would address the concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionability and realism of suggested revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When suggesting revisions in the review, think about whether the revisions are reasonable in terms of time and resources — which of the recommendations are essential, and which are nice-to-have but optional?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize suggestions as essential vs optional. Avoid demanding large new research programs or unrealistic experiments as a condition for acceptance; indicate what is required for the claim to hold versus future work ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the paper's story and problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the story of the paper clear? What is the problem that the paper aims to address?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper motivates the problem, states objectives and hypotheses clearly, and presents a coherent narrative. Point out missing or unclear motivation, and suggest ways to make the problem and goals more explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation relative to state-of-the-art limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the limitations in the state of the art that the paper addresses? Are the limitations clearly articulated, and reflective of the state of the art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the authors accurately characterize prior work and the gap they claim to fill. Flag overstatements about prior limitations or missed relevant prior work; suggest comparisons or citations that would contextualize the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of key novel technical contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the key novel technical contribution in the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask authors to state the core novelty succinctly. If the contribution is incremental or unclear, explain why and what would be needed to establish novelty (e.g., stronger theoretical analysis, new algorithmic idea, broader empirical evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and clarity of presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the technical approach sound and clearly described?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for errors, unstated assumptions, or missing details. Request missing proofs, derivations, hyperparameter settings, algorithm pseudocode, or implementation details that are necessary to assess correctness. Indicate whether the description is sufficient for a knowledgeable reader to understand the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / sufficiency of detail for reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it expressed in sufficient detail to permit reproduction of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand necessary details for reproducing experiments (architectures, seeds, datasets, preprocessing, hyperparameters, evaluation scripts). Note missing supplementary materials, code, or instructions; classify reproducibility issues as critical if they prevent verifying claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statement of limitations and generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper clearly describe the limitations (in scope and generalizability) of its conclusions? (All work has limits, and it is vital to understand them.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage honest discussion of scope, failure modes, assumptions, and contexts where the method may not apply. Flag papers that overclaim or omit important caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related work placement and contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed contribution placed in the appropriate context of previous and related work, so as to allow a reader to draw connections between this work and others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for missing relevant citations, insufficient comparison to prior methods, or failure to explain how the current work differs or improves on prior art. Suggest specific papers or threads of literature that should be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: appropriate baselines and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the empirical evaluation include appropriate baselines and comparisons to validate the proposed approach compared to the state of the art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing or weak baselines. Recommend standard or strong competitors and ablations that would clarify the contribution. Note whether hyperparameters for baselines are tuned fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the empirical evaluation report well-established and reasonable metrics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reported metrics actually measure the claimed advantages. Suggest additional or alternative metrics if current ones are insufficient or misleading (e.g., reporting accuracy alone when calibration or robustness matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of benchmarks and datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the evaluation benchmarks and datasets appropriately chosen? Are there any better benchmarks or datasets that should have been used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether datasets are realistic, sufficiently challenging, or biased. Recommend more appropriate datasets or cross-dataset evaluations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper include an analysis of errors made by the proposed approach?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for qualitative and quantitative analyses of failure modes, per-class/per-case breakdowns, and investigation into when and why the method fails. Recommend diagnostic experiments to illuminate weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicability of evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the evaluations fully replicable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for availability of code, seeds, splits, and full experimental details. If not replicable, indicate missing pieces and classify their importance for verifying claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive, prioritized suggestions for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: How could the research or the presentation of the paper be improved in light of the above?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a prioritized list of concrete improvements (e.g., revise explanation, add ablation, run on X dataset). Distinguish between essential fixes required for acceptance and optional improvements for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of reviewer content (no duplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers must not duplicate content from other reviews (neither the AI-generated nor human reviews), but are free to express their level of agreement with the points raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write original text and analyses rather than copying existing reviews. If agreeing with another review, summarize agreement in your own words and add any distinct perspective or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and use of AI-generated reviews and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-26 will include an AI-generated review in Phase 1 (without ratings or recommendations) and an AI-generated summary at the end of discussion. The AI-generated review will be clearly labelled as such and becomes visible to reviewers and authors at specified times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the AI review has no ratings/recommendations and is an aid: reviewers may read and reflect on it and may update their reviews accordingly, but must not copy content. SPCs and ACs will use AI reviews and summaries as one input among others when making promotion and decision recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging issues with AI-generated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers will have the ability to make an official comment on the AI-generated review (distinct from the reviewer discussion), along with review ratings. These comments will only be visible to SPCs and higher. The Program Chairs, Workflow chairs, and Area Chairs will monitor comments made on AI-generated reviews to identify issues, and will take action as appropriate, such as re-generating the review, or excluding it entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an AI-generated review is factually incorrect, misleading, or problematic, use the official comment mechanism rather than public discussion. Provide specific evidence for the complaint to assist SPCs/ACs in remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of review timeline and visibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-26 uses a two-phase reviewing process. Phase 1: two human reviews plus an AI-generated review (no ratings). Phase 2: additional human reviewers and an AI-generated summary at the end of discussion. Visibility of AI reviews varies by phase and decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware when AI reviews and other reviewers' comments become visible (to ACs, SPCs, reviewers, and authors) so you can appropriately time updates to your review and responses to rebuttals. Use the rebuttal period to reflect and update reviews if misunderstandings are clarified.
